column1: # tf-managed-role-allowlist.tsv — the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the Azure
# built-in role definitions the MG-23 dev infra-apply identity is permitted to
# grant and revoke inside meatgeek-v2-dev-rg.
# WHY THIS FILE AND NOT THE HCL (single-derivation discipline)
# Two artifacts need this list and they MUST agree:
#   1. apps/infrastructure/bootstrap/bootstrap.sh — builds the ABAC condition on
#      the apply identity's "Role Based Access Control Administrator" grant FROM
#      THIS FILE. The condition allowlists these role-definition GUIDs on both the
#      roleAssignments WRITE and DELETE actions.
#   2. apps/infrastructure/scripts/tf-static-checks.sh (CHECK 13) — diffs this
#      file against every `role_definition_name` in the Terraform graph, so adding
#      a role to the graph FAILS AT PR TIME with a clear message instead of
#      mid-apply with AuthorizationFailed and a partially-applied stack.
# Deriving the condition directly from the .tf files would mean bootstrap.sh had
# to parse HCL, and deriving the CI check from bootstrap.sh would mean CI had to
# execute it. One committed file that both READ is the same single-derivation
# discipline as scripts/state-account-name.sh (one derivation of the state-account
# name) and environments/backend-dev.hcl (one backend definition).
# HOW THE ROLE SET WAS ENUMERATED — FROM THE GRAPH, NEVER FROM A PLAN
#   grep -rn 'role_definition_name' apps/infrastructure --include='*.tf'
# This deliberately includes COUNT-DISABLED resources. A `terraform plan`
# UNDER-ENUMERATES: `azurerm_role_assignment.functions_app_deploy_publisher` and
# `modules/functions` `deploy_principal_deployment_container` are guarded by
# `var.app_deploy_principal_object_id != ""`, and the whole native_otlp module is
# count-guarded, so a plan taken while those guards are OFF omits roles that a
# later plan WILL require. An allowlist built from such a plan fails closed
# mid-apply the first time a guard flips. Re-run the grep above (not a plan)
# whenever the graph changes.
# GUID COLUMN — RESOLVED LIVE, COMMITTED AFTERWARDS
# An ABAC condition matches on the role-definition GUID, not the display name.
# The GUID column ships as PENDING. bootstrap.sh resolves each GUID LIVE:
#   az role definition list --name "<role>" --query "[0].name" -o tsv
# and FAILS CLOSED if a committed (non-PENDING) GUID disagrees with the live one
# — a disagreement means either the tenant resolves a different definition or the
# committed value is wrong, and silently preferring either would author a
# condition that does not mean what it reads. After a bootstrap run, commit the
# paste-ready resolved file bootstrap.sh emits.
# NEVER hardcode a remembered GUID here or in bootstrap.sh. Remembered Azure role
# GUIDs are a well-known source of silent, invisible authorization errors.
# HONEST SCOPE OF THE CI GUARD
# tf-static-checks.sh CHECK 13 guards role NAMES only. GUID correctness is a LIVE
# bootstrap-time property: a credential-less CI job cannot call Azure and so
# cannot re-verify it. The live verification lives in bootstrap.sh (fail-closed
# comparison) and in the operator acceptance tests T1/T2/T4 documented in
# docs/infrastructure/mg23-live-acceptance.md.
# WHAT THE CONDITION DOES AND DOES NOT CONSTRAIN
# The condition constrains WHICH role definition and WHICH principal type may be
# granted. It CANNOT constrain SCOPE: an allowlisted role can still be re-granted
# resource-group-wide inside meatgeek-v2-dev-rg (accepted residual F4), and Cosmos
# data-plane `sqlRoleAssignments` are Contributor-granted and invisible to a
# Microsoft.Authorization condition entirely (accepted residual F6). Both are
# recorded in docs/infrastructure/mg23-live-acceptance.md; do NOT read this file
# as claiming otherwise.
# FORMAT: <role_definition_name>\t<role_definition_guid|PENDING>
# Tab-separated. Lines beginning with # and blank lines are ignored.
Azure Event Hubs Data Receiver
SignalR Service Owner
Monitoring Metrics Publisher
Website Contributor
Storage Blob Data Owner
Storage Queue Data Contributor
Storage Blob Data Contributor
Azure Event Hubs Data Sender
